correctness.rationale: With at most two pebbles, after a move there is at most one stationary vertex to match, and every vertex on a board with both sides at least two has a neighbor and a distinct nonneighbor. For equal capped parameters at k>=3, after removal of a pebble at most k-1 coordinates on each axis are in use. Matching each axis by its own partial bijection preserves equality and sharing a coordinate; a fresh paired value exists on a small axis by exact equal sizes and on a large axis because its size is at least k. This works for arbitrarily many rounds. A clique of size at least three must share one coordinate, and an independent set changes both coordinates in every pair; maximum sizes are max(a,b) and min(a,b). Clique and independent-set formulas with up to k variables recover both truncated sizes. Counting the unordered truncated pairs, minimizing their products within a class, and enlarging a largest side to witness non-definability below max(a,b)+1 give all stated corollaries. This is a relative width, not a defining width among all graphs. The frozen scripts and stdout are bounded corroboration inspected but not executed; the permanent strategy is the universal proof. The extensional checker prunes subsets and does not independently exhaust every clique for the common-coordinate assertion.
